dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim for multiresolution analysis of a 256-sample signal. CWT mode draws a color-mapped scalogram |W(a,b)| at 32 log-spaced scales for the Morlet, Mexican hat or Haar wavelet and overlays the dilated wavelet at a chosen scale and position. Haar DWT mode shows 1-5 levels of detail and approximation coefficients as time-aligned bar plots, applies a hard threshold to the details and reports the reconstructed signal's mean squared error.

learningObjectives: Explain why scale is inversely related to frequency, and convert between scale and pseudo-frequency with f = fc fs / a
Interpret a scalogram to locate a chirp's changing frequency, a tone's band and a transient's time of occurrence
Compare the time and frequency resolution of the Morlet, Mexican hat and Haar wavelets
Calculate Haar approximation and detail coefficients, and the number of coefficients at each level
Analyze how the number of levels and the hard threshold trade noise removal against signal distortion

misconceptions.misconception: Each bright stripe along a scalogram band is a separate event
misconceptions.correction: With a real wavelet W(a,b) follows the signal's oscillation, so |W| rises and falls twice per cycle of a steady tone
misconceptions.evidence: With two tones and the Morlet wavelet the 8 Hz band shows 16 bright patches per second, and W(a,b) changes sign 16 times as b moves across the 1 s signal

misconceptions.misconception: A larger threshold always removes more noise and gives a cleaner signal
misconceptions.correction: Hard thresholding also removes the coefficients that carry the signal, so the error has a minimum and then rises
misconceptions.evidence: For the noisy sine at L = 5 the error against the clean sine falls from 0.0821 (T = 0) to 0.0462 (T = 0.65) and rises to 0.0965 at T = 2.00

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Wavelet explorer. In CWT mode the top plot shows a 256-sample signal with the dilated wavelet at the selected scale and position overlaid in gold, and the lower plot is a color-mapped scalogram of |W(a,b)| with time on the x axis and 32 log-spaced scales (pseudo-frequency 3 to 96 Hz) on the y axis. In Haar DWT mode the top plot shows the input and the reconstructed signal, and bar plots show the detail coefficients of each level and the final approximation, with a hard threshold band and the mean squared error.

controls.label: Mode
controls.description: Switches between the CWT scalogram and the Haar DWT views

controls.label: Mother wavelet
controls.description: Chooses the CWT mother wavelet (CWT mode only)

controls.label: dB color scale
controls.description: Maps the top 40 dB of |W| to the color map instead of linear |W| (CWT mode only)

controls.label: Scale a
controls.description: Selects one of the 32 log-spaced scales (pseudo-frequency 96 Hz down to 3 Hz); the label shows a in samples

controls.label: Position b
controls.description: Sets the translation b of the overlaid wavelet in samples; the label shows b in seconds

controls.label: Levels L
controls.description: Number of Haar decomposition levels (DWT mode only)

controls.label: Threshold T
controls.description: Hard threshold: detail coefficients with |d| <= T are set to zero before reconstruction (DWT mode only)

visualElements.description: Signal plot: x(t) in blue with the dilated wavelet psi((t - b)/a) in gold (CWT), or the input, the reconstruction in maroon and the clean sine (DWT)
Scalogram |W(a,b)| with pseudo-frequency and scale axes, a color bar and a marker at the selected (b, a); click to select
Time-aligned bar plots of the detail coefficients d1..dL and the approximation aL, with the threshold band in red and zeroed coefficients in gray
Read-outs: scale, pseudo-frequency, W(a,b) and the row maximum (CWT); coefficients kept and mean squared errors (DWT)

model.description: Direct-convolution CWT of a mirror-extended 256-sample signal at 32 log-spaced scales with 1/sqrt(a) normalization, and an orthonormal Haar DWT with hard thresholding of the detail coefficients and inverse transform
equations: Morlet: psi(t) = exp(-t^2/2) cos(5t); Mexican hat: psi(t) = (1 - t^2) exp(-t^2/2)
hard threshold: d' = d if |d| > T, else 0
algorithms: Direct convolution CWT (recomputed only when the signal, wavelet or color scale changes)
limitations: Pseudo-frequency is approximate; with 1/sqrt(a) normalization the Mexican hat places an 8 Hz tone near 7 Hz
Coefficients near the ends at large scales are affected by the mirror extension

instructionalStrategies: Predict where a chirp's ridge appears before reading the row maximum
Compare the three mother wavelets on the same signal
Find the threshold and level that minimize the denoising error
extensions: Add a complex (analytic) Morlet wavelet so the scalogram shows a smooth envelope instead of stripes
Add soft thresholding and a noise-estimated universal threshold
